title: Core valuation-ring properties for a finite p-adic extension
statement: The valuation ring and maximal ideal in the first fourteen clauses of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] exist with all displayed ring, DVR, fraction-field and finite-residue properties, through the existence of a generator of the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Equip E with abv.toNormedField. The extension identity makes E a normed Q_l-algebra, hence ultrametric, and supplies a norm greater than one from Q_l. FiniteDimensional.proper makes E proper. Its valuation integer ring is the closed unit ball, so is compact.

Apply the compact-integer-ring version of the proper rank-one valued-field criterion, Valued.integer.compactSpace_iff_completeSpace_and_isDiscreteValuationRing_and_finite_residueField, to the valuation defined by the norm. This gives a DVR of integers and a finite residue field. Take O to be this integer subring and m to be its canonical maximal ideal.

The integer-ring API identifies membership with abv <= 1 and units with abv = 1; nonunits therefore give membership in m exactly when abv < 1. The local-ring, fraction-ring and DVR APIs give the remaining ring properties. A nonzero prime ideal in a PID is maximal and hence equals m. Choose an irreducible rho in O, which generates m. Valuation divisibility says x divides y exactly when abv(y) <= abv(x), so equality of the two principal ideals is equivalent to equality of their generator absolute values. Set r = abv(rho). Membership in (rho) bounds abv by r, and rho itself attains r. Any generator of m is irreducible and nonzero; conversely an element of absolute value r has the same principal ideal as rho. These are precisely the last two clauses.

lean.statement: theorem extension_integers_dvr_core (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (abv : AbsoluteValue E ℝ) (h_ext : ∀ a : ℚ_[l], abv (algebraMap ℚ_[l] E a) = ‖a‖) : ∃ O : Subring E, ∃ m : Ideal O, (∀ x : E, x ∈ O ↔ abv x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x : O, x ∈ m ↔ abv (x : E) < 1) ∧ (∀ x : O, IsUnit x ↔ abv (x : E) = 1) ∧ IsLocalRing O ∧ m.IsMaximal ∧ (∀ J : Ideal O, J.IsMaximal → J = m) ∧ IsFractionRing O E ∧ IsDiscreteValuationRing O ∧ IsPrincipalIdealRing O ∧ m ≠ ⊥ ∧ (∀ J : Ideal O, J.IsPrime ∧ J ≠ ⊥ ↔ J = m) ∧ Finite (O ⧸ m) ∧ (∃ r : ℝ, (∃ y : O, y ∈ m ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ abv (y : E) = r) ∧ (∀ y : O, y ∈ m → y ≠ 0 → abv (y : E) ≤ r) ∧ (∀ π : O, Ideal.span ({π} : Set O) = m ↔ π ≠ 0 ∧ abv (π : E) = r)) ∧ (∃ π : O, Ideal.span ({π} : Set O) = m)
